Rashi on Niddah 30b:1:1.hebrew: הא קתני נדה - דכל דמים שתראה, טמאים. ומשני: לכך הוזכר זכר, שאם תראה ליום ל"ד ותחזור ותראה ליום מ"א, תהא מקולקלת עד מ"ח. שכשראתה ליום ל"ד ללידתה, אמרינן טמאה, אע"ג דאכתי משכי ימי טוהר דזכר, מספקינן לה בלא ולד ותשב לנדה. וכי הדר חזיא ליום מ"א, שהוא ח' לראייתה, ותרצה להיות שומרת יום כנגד יום — אמרינן: ולד היה וזכר היה, וראייה דיום ל"ד דם טוהר היא, והשתא הוא דהויא תחלת נדה. והשתא מקלקלינן לה דלא טבלה עד מ"ח, שהוא ח' לראייה אחרונה. ואי לאו משום ספקא דזכר, הוה טבלה למחר ליום מ"ב, ממ"נ: אי לאו ולד הוא — הרי שומרת יום כנגד יום היא, ואי ולד הוא ונקבה היא — אכתי הוה דם טוהר עד שמונים; וספקא דזכר מקלקלא לה:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:1:1.english: Doesn't [the mishna] teach [the strictures of] a menstruating woman - That all blood that she sees [is] impure. And [the Gemara] answers: For this [reason] a male was mentioned, that if she sees [blood] on the thirty-fourth day and again sees [blood] on the forty-first day, she shall be ruined [in her purity status] until the forty-eighth [day]. For when she saw [blood] on the thirty-fourth day from her birth, we say [she is] impure; even though the days of purity of a male still extend [beyond then], we treat her as uncertain [that perhaps there was] no child, and she must observe [the days of] a menstruating woman. And when she sees [blood] again on the forty-first day, which is the eighth [day] from her [first] sighting, and she wants to be a woman who observes a day against a day — we say: There was a child and it was a male, and the sighting of the thirty-fourth day was blood of purity, and now is when the beginning of [her] menstruation is. And now we ruin [her purity status] so that she does not immerse until the forty-eighth [day], which is the eighth [day] from the last sighting. And if not for the uncertainty of a male, she would immerse tomorrow, on the forty-second day, in either case: if it was not a child — behold, she is a woman who observes a day against a day; and if it was a child and it was a female — it is still blood of purity until eighty [days]; and thus the uncertainty of a male ruins [her purity status].

Rashi on Niddah 30b:3:1.english: And similarly, with regard to a female - That is to say, the uncertainty of a female [birth] also ruins her [status with] this ruination.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:3:2.hebrew: עד פ"ח - דלא טבלה עד פ"ח, דאי הוה פשיטא לן דלאו ולד הוא, הואי טבלה למחר ביום פ"ב, דראיית פ"א באחד עשר יום שבין נדה לנדה היא. ומשום דמספקא לן דילמא ולד הוה, וראייה דיום ע"ד דם טהור הוה, והשתא הויא תחלת נדה, לא טבלה עד פ"ח:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:3:2.english: Until [the] eighty-eighth [day] - For she cannot immerse until [day] eighty-eight, for if it were clear to us that it was not a fetus, she would immerse on the next day, on day eighty-two, because the sighting of [day] eighty-one is within the eleven days that are between one niddah [period] and [another] niddah [period]. And because we are in doubt [that] perhaps it was a fetus, and the sighting of day seventy-four was pure blood, and now it is the beginning of niddah, she cannot immerse until [day] eighty-eight.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:4:1.hebrew: טימא וטיהר בזכר - מ' יום בין שתיהן, ז' לטומאה ול"ג יום לימי טוהר:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:4:1.english: [The verse] deemed [her] impure and deemed [her] pure in [the case of] a male - Forty days between both of them: seven [days] for impurity, and thirty-three days for the days of purity.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:6:1.hebrew: נתחייבו הריגה - ומתוך שעומדות ליהרג, ניסו בהם ויחדום לביאה, וקרעו שתיהם לסוף מ', ונמצא אחד זכר ואחד נקבה:
Rashi on Niddah 30b:6:1.english: They were sentenced to death - And since they were about to be executed, they experimented on them and designated them for intercourse; and they cut open both of them at the end of forty [days], and one was found [to be] a male and one a female.

Rashi on Niddah 30b:8:1.hebrew: תלד - דאם נקבה תלד (ויקרא י״ב:ה׳) קרא יתירא הוא, דמצי למכתב "ואם נקבה וטמאה שבועים", דהא כתיב לעיל "וילדה זכר":
Rashi on Niddah 30b:8:1.english: She gives birth - For [the phrase] "if she gives birth to a female" (Leviticus 12:5) is a superfluous verse, as it could have written "and if a female, then she shall be impure two weeks," since it is written above "and she gives birth to a male."
